voyage.name: Fluted Minaret Mosque
voyage.content: Elegant six-domed mosque built under Seljuk rule in 1230 and rebuilt in 1373 by the Hamidids. The minaret is 38 m tall.

voyage.name: Sehzade Korkut Mosque
voyage.alt: Broken Minaret Mosque, Kesik Minare Cami
voyage.content: This was first built as a Roman temple in the 2nd century AD, and in later centuries went back and forth between religions. The minaret was added in the early 13th during one such conversion, and in 1800 this was the only part to survive a fire. The mosque lay in ruins until rebuilt from 2018, re-opening in 2021.

voyage.name: Ethnographic Museum
voyage.content: Exhibits traditional arts and crafts.

voyage.name: Hıdırlık Tower
voyage.content: Built by the Romans in the 2nd century AD with a square base and circular upper storey, this was a bastion and lighthouse. Its present name indicates that it's the site of Hıdırellez on 5/6 May, a religious spring festival.

voyage.name: Atatürk House Museum
voyage.content: Atatürk stayed in Antalya in 1930, 1931 and 1935. This rebuilt mansion shows memorabilia of his times.

voyage.name: Antalya Museum
voyage.content: One of Turkey's largest museums, with 5000 items illustrating the history of the Mediterranean and Pamphylia regions. It's also a repository for some 25,000 items not on display.

voyage.name: Antalya Aquarium
voyage.content: Huge aquarium with display tanks and long viewing tunnel.

voyage.name: Sandland
voyage.content: Sand sculpture park open year round, lit up at night.

voyage.name: Aksu Dolphinarium
voyage.content: Sea lions and dolphins do their splashy stuff at 11:00 and 15:00. Extra charges to swim with them or have a dolphin take a photo of you. People may wish to consider the ethics of such attractions before visiting.

voyage.name: Antalya Zoo
voyage.content: Large spacious zoo park.

voyage.name: Tünek Tepe
voyage.content: A hilltop of 618 m with great views over the city and coast, reached by gondola cable car though you can drive or even hike up. Food and drink at the top station are a silly price. The cable car collapsed in April 2024.

voyage.name: Perge
voyage.content: Extensive ruins of a city which had its heyday 2nd to 3rd century AD under the Romans. The site has a colonnaded agora, theatre, stadium, temple to Artemis and two churches.

voyage.name: Kurşunlu Waterfall
voyage.content: Woodland park, the waterfalls are impressive in flow but dry to a trickle in summer. A firm path leads you past the best views but is not suitable with restricted mobility. There are refreshment stalls and a café/restaurant.

voyage.name: King's Pool
voyage.content: An attractive pool in a canyon.

voyage.name: Aspendos
voyage.content: Graeco-Roman city, of which the centrepiece is the well-preserved amphitheatre, seating 7000. There's also 2 km of aqueduct (which siphoned water over rises), a stadium, baths, basilica, agora and nymphaeum. 1 km downstream near the modern highway is Eurymedon Bridge, rebuilt in wonky fashion in the 13th century when the Roman original washed away.

voyage.name: TerraCity
voyage.content: - A shopping center, in the east side of the city towards Lara beach strip, with some 180 stores and several restaurants.

voyage.name: Piyazcı Sami
voyage.content: Antalya-style piyaz (bean salad), kofte and other authentic fare.

voyage.name: Urfali Ciğercİ Apo
voyage.content: Simple place with good food.

voyage.name: Özkan Kebap
voyage.content: Good menu selection, budget place popular with locals.

voyage.name: Çiğköfteci Ömer Usta
voyage.content: Friendly place for çiğ köfte, raw meatballs.

voyage.name: Gizem Cafe Fast Food
voyage.content: Inexpensive place for trad shawarma and dürüm.

voyage.name: Köfteci
voyage.content: Authentically shabby place for Turkish trad food.

voyage.name: Public Konyaaltı
voyage.content: Within the main square on Konyaalti west beach strip, this serves burgers, thin-crust pizza and other filling food.

voyage.name: Yamaçoba
voyage.address: Heniye Hanım Apt 283 D/2, Atatürk Blv, Konyaaltı
voyage.content: Great quality for inexpensive food at the west end of the beach strip.

voyage.name: Bolero Büfe
voyage.address: Sultan Aprt, Güzeloba, Lara Cd. No:188/Be
voyage.content: Serving lamb, chicken and other meat kebabs. Garlic mayo is available on request.

voyage.name: Rokka Pizza Falafel
voyage.content: Good eating place with lots of veggie / vegan choices.

voyage.name: Ayar Meyhanesi
voyage.content: Friendly restaurant with a great selection of fresh fish. The swimming pool is a puzzle, is it a vivarium where lobsters choose which human bather to eat?

voyage.name: Paradise Restaurant
voyage.content: Sports bar with decent food.

voyage.name: Grand Friends
voyage.content: Fish and steak to a high standard, friendly service.

voyage.name: Karaf Bistro Kaleiçi
voyage.content: Pleasant relaxing place with pizza and wine. The owner's cat won't steal your wine but will try to claim its share of everything else.

voyage.name: Hasanağa
voyage.content: Long-established family-run restaurant, pleasant garden setting and great trad food.

voyage.name: Seraser
voyage.content: Fine dining which they mostly deliver, but at these prices they need to be more consistent.

voyage.name: Whitegarden Hotel
voyage.content: Gorgeous little place in old town.

voyage.name: Sibel Pansiyon
voyage.content: Welcoming hotel owned by a warmhearted multilingual French woman. Rooms have aircon, satellite TV and private bathrooms. It's quiet at night, good breakfasts.

voyage.name: Hotel Blue Sea Garden
voyage.content: Friendly hotel with garden restaurant. Some rooms dark and dingy, others pleasant with sea view.

voyage.name: Alp Paşa Hotel
voyage.content: Atmospheric hotel in the historic district with good restaurant.

voyage.name: Tuvana Hotel
voyage.content: Pleasant peaceful hotel near centre, with 45 rooms and small pool.

voyage.name: DoubleTree by Hilton
voyage.content: Mid-range chain hotel north end of downtown, mostly good reviews.

voyage.name: Hotel Su
voyage.content: Quirky decor, good service and comfort.

voyage.name: Pearly Hotel
voyage.content: Facing the beach. Many fittings in need of repair.

voyage.name: Megasaray Westbeach
voyage.content: Great reviews for this beachfront hotel.

voyage.name: Akra Hotels
voyage.content: Smart efficient hotel, limited sea access.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Lara
voyage.content: 1 km from beach, good value.

voyage.name: Lara Barut
voyage.content: Great reviews for this upmarket family-oriented hotel.

voyage.name: Delphin Imperial
voyage.content: Great reviews for comfort and service.

voyage.name: Grand Park Lara
voyage.content: Small rooms, some lapses, but overall good value for the price.

voyage.name: Concorde De Luxe Resort
voyage.content: Consistently good reviews for comfort and service.

voyage.name: Sherwood Exclusive Lara
voyage.content: Fair value from this mid-price place.

voyage.name: Royal Seginus Hotel
voyage.content: Comfy enough, but poor scores for noise and catering.

voyage.name: Baia Lara
voyage.content: Service, cleanliness and catering erratic.

voyage.name: Aska Lara Resort
voyage.content: Family-oriented hotel with lots of children's activities.

voyage.name: Kremlin Palace
voyage.content: It's supposed to recreate the luxury of a Russian tsar, with a hoaky St Basil's overlooking the pool. Good reviews.

voyage.name: Swandor Topkapi Palace
voyage.content: Mixed reviews, some guests have a great stay, others find comfort, service and food way below standard.

voyage.name: Titanic Mardan Palace
voyage.content: Great scores for comfort and service. The swimming pool is huge.

voyage.name: Trendy Lara
voyage.content: Huge family-oriented hotel.

voyage.name: Awen Lara
voyage.content: Huge family-oriented hotel.
